That is, \( C = \{e^{2\pi i k / 18} e^{2\pi i m / 48} : k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, 17 \text{ and } m = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, 47\} \). This can be simplified to \( C = \{e^{2\pi i (16k + 3m) / 144} : k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, 17 \text{ and } m = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, 47\} \).

Note that \( 16k + 3m \) will take on all possible values modulo 144 as \( k \) and \( m \) range from 0 to 17 and 0 to 47 respectively. This is because 16 and 3 are coprime to 144, and so the combinations of 16k and 3m will cover all residues modulo 144. Therefore, the set \( C \) will have 144 distinct elements.

Thus, the number of distinct elements in \( C \) is \( \boxed{144} \).
